assessment: No production Stage 2 identity module is present at the inspected base. These cases therefore distinguish an observed weakness in the current Stage 1 test helper from pre-implementation requirements for Lane 02. They do not claim a nonexistent runtime has failed.

cases.observed_repository_fact: tests/test_contract_schemas.py load_json() uses json.loads() without an object_pairs_hook, while canonical_bytes() hashes the already-parsed Python value.
cases.observed_effect: Standard Python json.loads collapses input_a to the same parsed object as input_b, so hashing after parse cannot distinguish the ambiguous duplicate-member source from the unambiguous source.
cases.required_oracle: The production Stage 2 loader must reject duplicate JSON object member names before canonical identity is derived. It must not silently last-wins or first-wins an ambiguous source document.

cases.current_helper_observation: The current helper preserves Unicode code points and therefore produces different UTF-8 canonical bytes/hashes for NFC and NFD spellings. That behavior is deterministic, but the repository does not yet declare whether canonical identity intentionally preserves code-point form or normalizes it.
cases.required_oracle: Stage 2 must make Unicode normalization policy explicit and regression-tested. Either exact code-point preservation or an explicit normalization form may be chosen, but host/parser/editor normalization must never silently decide immutable identity.
cases.continuity_question: Can a fresh occupant determine from repository state alone whether canonically equivalent-looking text should share or differ in immutable identity?

cases.scenario: A valid object omits an optional property whose JSON Schema contains a default annotation. One implementation hashes the exact validated input; another validator mutates the instance by inserting defaults before hashing.
cases.required_oracle: Canonicalization must not depend on validator-specific default insertion. For v0, any default materialization policy must be explicit, deterministic, and stored/tested; absent that policy, identity should be derived from the explicit validated instance rather than silently synthesized fields.
cases.failure_if_unresolved: Two occupants using different validator behavior can derive different immutable identities from the same repository document without either seeing an error.

cases.scenario: Two different kernel object kinds can theoretically have identical canonical content bytes or a caller can present only a bare digest without object kind, schema version, or hash-algorithm context. A later occupant must guess what the digest is supposed to identify.
cases.required_oracle: An immutable reference used for provenance, evidence, replay, or supersession must be self-describing enough for deterministic parsing or be accompanied by explicit stored type/schema/algorithm context. A bare digest must not become an undocumented universal reference convention.
cases.implementation_boundary: Lane 02 still owns the exact encoding. This oracle constrains meaning, not string syntax.

positive_controls.observed: The current test helper uses sort_keys=true, so parsed objects with different member order canonicalize identically. Preserve equivalent deterministic behavior in the production Stage 2 implementation.

The current test helper uses allow_nan=false, so Python NaN/Infinity values are rejected during JSON serialization. Production canonicalization should remain strict JSON rather than introducing non-standard numeric tokens.
